title: Thrill Rides for Teens: The Best Coaster Parks to Visit
description: The best theme parks for thrill-seeking teenagers in the UK, Europe and the US, plus height rules, queue hacks and keeping the whole family happy.
h1: Thrill rides for teens: the best coaster parks
intro: Got a coaster-obsessed teenager? These are the parks with the biggest drops, loops and launches, plus tips to keep younger siblings and nervous parents happy too.

image.alt: Riders with arms in the air on a roller coaster

cardText: Big drops, launches and loops, plus height rules and queue hacks.

blocks.title: Scout’s thrill tip
blocks.text: Teens can often ride in their own group while parents do gentler rides with siblings. Agree a meeting point and time before you split up.
points: Check height limits on the park website
Ride the biggest coaster first thing

sections.html:
• Thorpe Park (Surrey): built around big thrill rides.
  • Alton Towers (Staffordshire): famous coasters plus areas for little ones.
  • Blackpool Pleasure Beach (Lancashire): historic wooden coasters and big modern rides.

See all theme parks and the Merlin pass.

• Phantasialand (Germany) and Europa-Park (Germany) for richly themed coasters.
  • PortAventura (Spain), including Ferrari Land.
  • Cedar Point (Ohio), a legendary coaster park, and Universal Orlando for themed thrills.

Read Europe’s best theme parks.

Every ride has a minimum height (and some a maximum). They’re strict, so measure before you go and check the park’s ride guide. People with certain medical conditions are often advised not to ride intense coasters: read the signs at each ride.
Arrive before opening, use single rider lines and save the big ride for the last hour too. More in theme park queue tips.

faqs.q: What is the best UK theme park for teenagers?
faqs.a: Thorpe Park and Alton Towers are the UK’s best-known thrill parks, with Blackpool Pleasure Beach another favourite.

faqs.q: Can teenagers go round a theme park alone?
faqs.a: Rules vary. Many parks require under-16s or under-14s to be accompanied. Check the park’s age policy.
